text:
sam: Quick proposal for span naming + attributes for LLM inference spans. TL;DR: keep span.name super stable/low-cardinality and surface model/size/token/cache info as semantic attributes. Trying to avoid cardinality explosion in traces and keep dashboards sane.

maria: +1 on low-cardinality names. Can you sketch concrete attr names? we need them to map to dashboards and routing rules.

sam: Sure — draft below. Two goals: 1) minimal span.name (for grouping) 2) well-scoped attrs for dashboards/alerts/exports. Example pattern: 

```
span.name = "inference.call"           # generic grouping across flows
span.kind = "client"/"server"        # existing OTEL kind

# Semantic attrs (OTEL string/number/bool)
redwood.model.name = "llama2-13b"     # stable model identifier
redwood.model.variant = "q4_0"        # quantization / runtime variant
redwood.model.repo = "hf/llama2"    # optional, low-cardinality if used sparingly

redwood.request.route = "api.generate" # route/service-level path
redwood.routing.policy = "latency-preferred" # policy used

redwood.tokens.prompt = 56              # user input tokens (int)
redwood.tokens.generated = 240          # response tokens (int)
redwood.tokens.cache_saved = 120        # saved tokens via prefix/KV cache (int)

redwood.cache.kv_hits = 3               # number of KV hits (int)
redwood.cache.kv_misses = 0             # misses (int)
redwood.cache.prefix_hit = true         # boolean if prefix cache matched

redwood.cost.estimate_usd = 0.0012      # optional, low-cardinality metric
redwood.fallback.used = "model-b"     # if fallback was used (only set on fallback)
```

josh: Nice. A couple of thoughts:
- keep `redwood.model.repo` optional — customers can create high-cardinality if they put branches in names, so maybe we need a whitelist.
- `redwood.fallback.used` as string could explode; maybe set boolean `redwood.fallback` + `redwood.fallback_rank` (int) or leave string but tag as sampled.

lia: From exporter/ES side: numeric attrs are great for aggregations. For logs/dashboards we want a composite id to join traces -> logs. Can we add `redwood.request.id` (uuid) but mark it as not indexed by default?

sam: Agreed on whitelist and sampling. Updated constraints:
- Only `redwood.model.name` and `redwood.model.variant` allowed in default exports. Anything else must be explicitly enabled per env.
- `redwood.fallback.used` -> keep as boolean `redwood.fallback` and `redwood.fallback_reason` only on sampled/failure traces.
- `redwood.request.id` emitted always but set as `trace_id` fallback; exporters should treat it as non-indexed tag by default.

ingest-bot: Note: export pipeline currently drops attributes > 128 chars and only exports 50 custom attributes per span to Datadog. Will need a pipeline step to filter/rename.

maria: Good call. We also need a stable naming doc for console metrics: mapping suggestions for dashboards: 
- latency p95: filter span.name=inference.call and routing.policy=latency-preferred
- cost per request: sum(redwood.cost.estimate_usd) grouped by model.variant
- cache hit rate: sum(redwood.cache.kv_hits) / sum(redwood.cache.kv_hits + redwood.cache.kv_misses)

josh: One more: we should define sampling rules that keep high-traffic models at higher sampling and rare model names fully sampled for debug. Also annotate `sample.reason` attr: e.g., "error", "debug-high-sample", "policy-keep".

sam: Next steps I propose:
1) Lock span.name to "inference.call" for all frontends + add a single span.role attr for surface differentiation (client/edge/backend).
2) Add attribute whitelist and sampling knobs in ingest pipeline config (eng-infra to implement).
3) Draft a short console doc mapping attrs -> dashboards/alerts.
4) Small RFC for export limits (Datadog/ES) and renaming rules.

lia: LGTY. I'll open a tiny RFC and add the pipeline task in the backlog.

maria: :thumbsup: please include examples for log-join (trace_id vs redwood.request.id).

sam: will do — I'll post the RFC link once created. Thanks all.

ingest-bot: Deploy note: new attr whitelist will be gated behind feature-flag `telemetry_attr_whitelist_v1`.
